data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 318 recorded a material favourable prior-year reserve movement in 2019: gross claims provisions reduced by GBP 132.237m (50.1% of the opening gross claims outstanding), driven principally by favourable claims development and a lower incidence of catastrophe activity. The improvement is reported as applying to the 2017 and prior years of account. Notable current-year events included Hurricane Dorian (estimated net cost ~GBP 7m) while prior-year deterioration references include Hawaii lava flow and California wildfire losses affecting property binders. The overall direction of prior-year movement is a release.
raw_causal_phrases: There have been positive reserve movements in the year, on the 2017 and prior years of account.
In 2019 there has been an improvement of GBP 5.2m on closed year reserves

Favourable movements of GBP 10.3 million, (2018: GBP 13.8 million), in the past year's provision for claims outstanding and IBNR, net of expected reinsurance recoveries, are included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance.
There has been significant deteriorations in reserves on the losses in Hawaii from lava flow, and the California Wildfire losses.
The only catastrophe loss of note in the year was Hurricane Dorian which is estimated at GBP 7m (US$9m).

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development taken from Note 17 'Change in prior year provisions' (Insurance liabilities / gross column). Opening reserves taken from the balance sheet prior-year comparative. The report also quotes net (after reinsurance) movements and contains RITC items for closed years (2017 RITC) elsewhere; gross figures were preferred and used. Amounts for specific events (e.g. Hawaii, California wildfires, Ethiopian Airlines) are discussed qualitatively and not quantified in the gross prior-year movement note; where only net figures are present in narrative these were ignored in favour of gross movement note.
